title: The resource cost of magic in a code block
abstract: We bound the magic of a post-selected logical measurement by the resource that produced it. The setting is one code block with one logical qubit and an adaptive protocol that measures, feeds forward and accepts. The witness reads the accepted effect against the free set of the resource theory of magic, outcome by outcome and not on the averaged channel, since a channel can be free while one of its outcomes measures the magic axis. Our first bound is unconditional. The accepted magic is at most a constant times the summed distance of the cells from the free set. The second is the main result. When the resource cells sit inside a bounded-spread exact-recovery skeleton, the recovery puts every insertion history below a threshold onto a single free branch, transcript by transcript, so only connected clusters reaching the threshold contribute and an exact-component expansion controls their weight. With a threshold linear in the code distance, polynomially many cells of bounded insertion degree and per-cell dilation amplitude $O(1/d)$, the accepted magic times the acceptance probability is at most $\exp[-Ω(d\log d)]$. Post-selection is disposed of before accepted transcripts are summed, so a branch of vanishing probability cannot be amplified into a magic effect. The threshold is certified from a circuit, and we run it on one exact round of stabilizer measurement followed by a split readout, which measures logical $X$ on the accepted fibre and logical $Z$ on the rejected ones. That certifies a threshold equal to the code distance for every single-layer pattern of weak $Z$-rotations, one per data qubit, so the hypotheses are met by a family and not one design. A member carries magic only if its support contains a logical $Z$ string. One member attains the exponent, again at the level of the accepted effect. Suppression is set by the threshold and not by the topology of the block.
summary: This theoretical work derives a tight upper bound on the resource cost ('magic') associated with post-selected logical measurements in quantum error-correcting codes. By analyzing the accepted effect through an outcome-by-outcome resource theory lens, the authors prove the cost decays exponentially with the code distance, $\exp[-\Omega(d \log d)]$. This result is significant because it quantifies the fundamental resource limitations for implementing complex quantum operations.
main_problem: The paper aims to rigorously bound the resource cost, or 'magic,' associated with performing a post-selected logical measurement within a quantum code block.
main_result: The accepted magic, when multiplied by the acceptance probability, is bounded by $\exp[-\Omega(d \log d)]$, a bound that is shown to be attainable by a specific protocol.
method: The analysis employs resource theory techniques, reading the accepted effect outcome-by-outcome against the free set of magic, and utilizes exact-component expansions over connected clusters of insertion histories.
model_or_system: The system is a single code block encoding one logical qubit, analyzed using an adaptive protocol involving measurement, feed-forward, and acceptance, relevant to fault-tolerant quantum computation.
key_observables: Magic (resource cost), Acceptance Probability, Code Distance ($d$), and the resulting bound $\exp[-\Omega(d \log d)]$.
important_parameters: Code distance ($d$), the certified threshold ($D \propto d$), and the structure of the exact-recovery skeleton.
main_assumptions: The resource cells must sit inside a bounded-spread exact-recovery skeleton, and the analysis relies on the structure of the accepted effect being read outcome-by-outcome.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the operations of a split-readout family, detailing syndrome measurement, classical recording, and the separation into accepted and rejected measurement fibres.
paper_structure: The paper develops bounds by first establishing an unconditional bound, then presenting the main result using an exact-component expansion. It certifies the threshold using a circuit model (stabilizer measurement followed by split readout) and concludes by showing a protocol that attains the derived exponential bound.
why_interesting: It provides a quantitative, resource-theoretic understanding of the fundamental limitations on measurement fidelity and resource consumption in fault-tolerant quantum computation, which is crucial for designing practical quantum hardware.

A single exact round of stabilizer measurement follows and writes its outcomes to a classical record. Everything after the dashed cut reads that record and nothing else. If the record matches the syndrome the block came in with, the protocol measures the logical X and keeps the +1 outcome, and that branch is the accepted fibre whose effect this paper bounds.
